+The homepage loads `analytics.js` with `defer`. It records an initial
+`page_view`, another view after a back/forward cache restore, and delegated
+`click` events (including clicks on nested elements inside links).
+
+Configure the deployment to accept JSON POSTs at `/api/analytics`. This static
+repository does not implement a collector. The payload is `{ "events": [...] }`;
+each event contains `type`, a Unix millisecond `timestamp`, and `page` (pathname
+only, capped at 256 characters). Clicks also include the target tag, containing
+section, and zero-based interactive-element index within that section (`-1`
+for other targets). No cookies, text content, query strings, or field values
+are included.
+
+Events debounce for 10 seconds, with a 30-second maximum wait. Batches are
+bounded to 50 events and 48 KiB of JSON. Native `fetchLater` replaces the
+pending snapshot on each interaction and can send on departure. Unsupported
+browsers or native quota errors use a timer and a hidden-page flush with a
+low-priority keepalive fetch. Collection never blocks navigation. Delivery is
+best effort, without persistent storage or retries; offline or rejected requests
+may be lost.

+# Daily Grind analytics
+
+The homepage loads `analytics.js` with `defer`. It records a `page_view` on load
+(and when restored from the back/forward cache), plus delegated `click` events
+on links, buttons, and elements with `role="button"`.
+
+Provide a same-origin `POST /api/analytics` receiver in the hosting backend.
+This static repository does not implement that endpoint. Requests contain JSON:
+
+```json
+{"events":[{"type":"page_view","timestamp":"2026-11-11T00:00:00.000Z","path":"/"},{"type":"click","timestamp":"2026-11-11T00:00:01.000Z","path":"/","element":"a","destination":"/menu"}]}
+```
+
+Events are sent after 600 ms without another event, with a five-second maximum
+wait during continuous activity and a 50-event batch limit. When the document
+is hidden or left, pending events use `sendBeacon`, falling back to a keepalive
+fetch if the beacon is unavailable or rejected. Normal batches use asynchronous
+keepalive fetch. Empty queues do not send requests. Delivery is best effort;
+failed batches are dropped without retries or disruption to navigation.
+
+No text content, query strings, fragments, external destinations, cookies, or
+persistent user identifiers are added to event data. Paths should not contain
+sensitive information. The receiver is responsible for validation and storage.
+
+Run the isolated client behavior tests with `npm test`; no server is required.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+Static homepage with browser-encrypted delivery notes. Run `pnpm install` and `pnpm build` to rebuild the committed `assets/delivery-notes.js` bundle. `pnpm test` checks encryption, tampering, key persistence, and deletion without starting a server.
+
+## Delivery notes
+
+- Hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 is the default. Standalone ML-KEM-768 and classical X25519 (ECDH P-256 fallback) are available under protection settings.
+- Native WebCrypto KEMs are capability-detected. The pinned, bundled `@noble/post-quantum` implementation preserves hybrid/post-quantum protection when native KEM APIs are unavailable. No runtime CDN scripts or plaintext fallback are used.
+- Each note uses a fresh recipient key pair and encapsulation/ephemeral key agreement. HKDF-SHA-256 derives a non-exportable AES-256-GCM key with a random salt and application-specific context. Each encryption uses a random 96-bit IV and a 128-bit tag. Version, record/recipient ID, suite, cipher, creation time, capsule, and salt are authenticated as additional data.
+- IndexedDB atomically stores ciphertext and the local recipient key. Native private keys are non-exportable CryptoKeys. Library private bytes are wrapped with AES-GCM under a non-exportable CryptoKey before storage. Deletion removes both records.
+- HTTPS (or localhost) and IndexedDB are required. Controls remain disabled until initialization succeeds; encryption/storage errors never submit plaintext.
+
+This repository has no delivery backend or authenticated driver key directory. Notes are saved **only in this browser profile**, and are not attached to orders or sent to drivers. Anyone with access to the profile can reveal them. Encryption does not protect against malicious scripts running on the same origin. Clearing site data permanently removes notes and keys. Revealed notes hide after 30 seconds or when the tab becomes hidden.
+
+A future remote delivery integration must provision and authenticate the driver's public key separately, retain private keys on the recipient device, and transmit only the authenticated envelope over HTTPS. Do not send the local recipient or wrapping key to a backend.

+import { ml_kem768_x25519 } from '@noble/post-quantum/hybrid.js';
+import { ml_kem768 } from '@noble/post-quantum/ml-kem.js';
+
+const encoder = new TextEncoder();
+const random = (length) => crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(length));
+const bytes = (value) => new Uint8Array(value);
+export const suiteNames = {
+  hybrid: 'Hybrid · ML-KEM-768 + X25519',
+  quantum: 'Post-quantum · ML-KEM-768',
+  X25519: 'Classical · X25519',
+  'P-256': 'Classical · ECDH P-256',
+};
+const kems = { hybrid: ml_kem768_x25519, quantum: ml_kem768 };
+const nativeNames = { hybrid: 'MLKEM768-X25519', quantum: 'ML-KEM-768' };
+const encode = (data) => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes(data)));
+const decode = (data) => Uint8Array.from(atob(data), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0));
+const aad = (header) => encoder.encode(JSON.stringify(header));
+
+async function aesKey(secret, salt, header) {
+  try {
+    const base = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', secret, 'HKDF', false, ['deriveKey']);
+    return await crypto.subtle.deriveKey({ name: 'HKDF', hash: 'SHA-256', salt,
+      info: encoder.encode(`daily-grind/delivery-notes/v1/${header.suite}/${header.recipient}`) },
+    base, { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt']);
+  } finally { secret.fill(0); }
+}
+const dhAlgorithm = (suite) => suite === 'P-256' ? { name: 'ECDH', namedCurve: 'P-256' } : { name: 'X25519' };
+async function dhSecret(privateKey, publicKey, suite) {
+  return bytes(await crypto.subtle.deriveBits({ name: dhAlgorithm(suite).name, public: publicKey }, privateKey, 256));
+}
+
+// Each local note has its own recipient. Only its public key is used by the sender.
+export async function sealNote(text, protection = 'hybrid', { useNative = true } = {}) {
+  if (!text.trim() || text.length > 1000) throw new Error('Enter a note of 1–1,000 characters.');
+  if (!['hybrid', 'quantum', 'classical'].includes(protection)) throw new Error('Unknown protection mode.');
+  const id = crypto.randomUUID();
+  let suite = protection;
+  let recipient;
+  let capsule;
+  let secret;
+  if (protection === 'classical') {
+    suite = 'X25519';
+    let pair;
+    try { pair = await crypto.subtle.generateKey('X25519', false, ['deriveBits']); }
+    catch (error) {
+      if (error.name !== 'NotSupportedError') throw error;
+      suite = 'P-256';
+      pair = await crypto.subtle.generateKey(dhAlgorithm(suite), false, ['deriveBits']);
+    }
+    const publicBytes = await crypto.subtle.exportKey('raw', pair.publicKey);
+    const publicKey = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', publicBytes, dhAlgorithm(suite), true, []);
+    const ephemeral = await crypto.subtle.generateKey(dhAlgorithm(suite), false, ['deriveBits']);
+    capsule = bytes(await crypto.subtle.exportKey('raw', ephemeral.publicKey));
+    secret = await dhSecret(ephemeral.privateKey, publicKey, suite);
+    recipient = { id, suite, kind: 'dh', privateKey: pair.privateKey };
+  } else if (useNative && globalThis.SubtleCrypto?.supports?.('encapsulateBits', nativeNames[suite]) &&
+    globalThis.SubtleCrypto?.supports?.('decapsulateBits', nativeNames[suite])) {
+    const name = nativeNames[suite];
+    const pair = await crypto.subtle.generateKey(name, false, ['encapsulateBits', 'decapsulateBits']);
+    const publicBytes = await crypto.subtle.exportKey('raw-public', pair.publicKey);
+    const publicKey = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw-public', publicBytes, name, true, ['encapsulateBits']);
+    const result = await crypto.subtle.encapsulateBits(name, publicKey);
+    capsule = bytes(result.ciphertext);
+    secret = bytes(result.sharedKey);
+    recipient = { id, suite, kind: 'native', privateKey: pair.privateKey };
+  } else {
+    // Bundle the established KEM implementation instead of downgrading PQ protection.
+    const kem = kems[suite];
+    const pair = kem.keygen();
+    try {
+      const result = kem.encapsulate(pair.publicKey);
+      capsule = result.cipherText;
+      secret = result.sharedSecret;
+      // Do not persist raw KEM private bytes. The wrapping key is non-exportable.
+      const wrappingKey = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt']);
+      const wrappingIv = random(12);
+      const wrappedSecret = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv: wrappingIv,
+        additionalData: encoder.encode(`${id}/${suite}`) }, wrappingKey, pair.secretKey);
+      recipient = { id, suite, kind: 'library', wrappingKey, wrappingIv, wrappedSecret };
+    } finally { pair.secretKey.fill(0); }
+  }
+  const salt = random(32);
+  const iv = random(12);
+  const header = { version: 1, id, recipient: id, suite, cipher: 'AES-256-GCM',
+    created: new Date().toISOString(), capsule: encode(capsule), salt: encode(salt) };
+  const plaintext = encoder.encode(text);
+  try {
+    const key = await aesKey(secret, salt, header);
+    const ciphertext = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv, additionalData: aad(header), tagLength: 128 }, key, plaintext);
+    return { envelope: { header, iv: encode(iv), ciphertext: encode(ciphertext) }, recipient };
+  } finally { plaintext.fill(0); secret.fill(0); }
+}
+
+export async function openNote(envelope, recipient) {
+  const { header, iv, ciphertext } = envelope;
+  if (header.version !== 1 || header.cipher !== 'AES-256-GCM' || header.recipient !== recipient.id ||
+    header.id !== recipient.id || header.suite !== recipient.suite || !suiteNames[header.suite]) {
+    throw new Error('Invalid encrypted note.');
+  }
+  let secret;
+  if (recipient.kind === 'dh') {
+    const publicKey = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', decode(header.capsule), dhAlgorithm(header.suite), true, []);
+    secret = await dhSecret(recipient.privateKey, publicKey, header.suite);
+  } else if (recipient.kind === 'native') {
+    secret = bytes(await crypto.subtle.decapsulateBits(nativeNames[header.suite], recipient.privateKey, decode(header.capsule)));
+  } else if (recipient.kind === 'library' && kems[header.suite]) {
+    const privateBytes = bytes(await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv: recipient.wrappingIv,
+      additionalData: encoder.encode(`${recipient.id}/${recipient.suite}`) }, recipient.wrappingKey, recipient.wrappedSecret));
+    try { secret = kems[header.suite].decapsulate(decode(header.capsule), privateBytes); }
+    finally { privateBytes.fill(0); }
+  } else { throw new Error('Unknown recipient key.'); }
+  const key = await aesKey(secret, decode(header.salt), header);
+  const plaintext = bytes(await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv: decode(iv),
+    additionalData: aad(header), tagLength: 128 }, key, decode(ciphertext)));
+  try { return new TextDecoder().decode(plaintext); }
+  finally { plaintext.fill(0); }
+}

+import test from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { sealNote, openNote } from './crypto.js';
+
+for (const protection of ['hybrid', 'quantum', 'classical']) {
+  test(`${protection}: round trip, fresh encryption, and non-exportable stored keys`, async () => {
+    const text = 'Side door, code 0428. Please don’t ring. ☕';
+    const first = await sealNote(text, protection);
+    const second = await sealNote(text, protection);
+    assert.equal(await openNote(first.envelope, structuredClone(first.recipient)), text);
+    assert.notEqual(first.envelope.ciphertext, second.envelope.ciphertext);
+    assert.notEqual(first.envelope.iv, second.envelope.iv);
+    assert.notEqual(first.envelope.header.capsule, second.envelope.header.capsule);
+    assert.equal(JSON.stringify(first.envelope).includes(text), false);
+    const key = first.recipient.wrappingKey || first.recipient.privateKey;
+    assert.equal(key.extractable, false);
+    await assert.rejects(() => openNote(first.envelope, second.recipient));
+  });
+  test(`${protection}: rejects tampering with ciphertext and authenticated metadata`, async () => {
+    const { envelope, recipient } = await sealNote('Leave at the side door', protection);
+    for (const field of ['ciphertext', 'iv', 'capsule', 'salt', 'created', 'id', 'suite', 'version']) {
+      const changed = structuredClone(envelope);
+      if (field === 'created') changed.header.created = '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z';
+      else if (field === 'id') changed.header.id = crypto.randomUUID();
+      else if (field === 'suite') changed.header.suite = 'invalid';
+      else if (field === 'version') changed.header.version = 2;
+      else {
+        const target = ['ciphertext', 'iv'].includes(field) ? changed : changed.header;
+        const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(target[field]), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0));
+        bytes[0] ^= 1;
+        target[field] = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes));
+      }
+      await assert.rejects(() => openNote(changed, recipient), field);
+    }
+  });
+}
+test('bundled hybrid and post-quantum fallback round trips', async () => {
+  for (const mode of ['hybrid', 'quantum']) {
+    const result = await sealNote('No doorbell, please', mode, { useNative: false });
+    assert.equal(result.recipient.kind, 'library');
+    assert.equal(await openNote(result.envelope, result.recipient), 'No doorbell, please');
+    const wrong = structuredClone(result.recipient);
+    wrong.wrappedSecret = new Uint8Array(wrong.wrappedSecret);
+    wrong.wrappedSecret[0] ^= 1;
+    await assert.rejects(() => openNote(result.envelope, wrong));
+  }
+});
+test('rejects blank, oversized notes and unknown protection', async () => {
+  await assert.rejects(() => sealNote('   '));
+  await assert.rejects(() => sealNote('a'.repeat(1001)));
+  await assert.rejects(() => sealNote('A note', 'invalid'));
+});

+let database;
+export function openDatabase() {
+  if (database) return database;
+  database = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    const request = indexedDB.open('daily-grind-private-notes', 1);
+    request.onupgradeneeded = () => {
+      request.result.createObjectStore('notes', { keyPath: 'header.id' });
+      request.result.createObjectStore('recipients', { keyPath: 'id' });
+    };
+    request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);
+    request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
+    request.onblocked = () => reject(new Error('Close other Daily Grind tabs and reload.'));
+  });
+  return database;
+}
+async function transaction(stores, mode, action) {
+  const db = await openDatabase();
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    const tx = db.transaction(stores, mode);
+    let result;
+    action(tx, (value) => { result = value; });
+    tx.oncomplete = () => resolve(result);
+    tx.onerror = () => reject(tx.error);
+    tx.onabort = () => reject(tx.error || new Error('Storage operation was cancelled.'));
+  });
+}
+export const listNotes = () => transaction(['notes'], 'readonly', (tx, done) => {
+  tx.objectStore('notes').getAll().onsuccess = (event) => done(event.target.result);
+});
+export const getRecipient = (id) => transaction(['recipients'], 'readonly', (tx, done) => {
+  tx.objectStore('recipients').get(id).onsuccess = (event) => done(event.target.result);
+});
+export const saveNote = ({ envelope, recipient }) => transaction(['notes', 'recipients'], 'readwrite', (tx) => {
+  tx.objectStore('notes').put(envelope);
+  tx.objectStore('recipients').put(recipient);
+});
+export const deleteNote = (id) => transaction(['notes', 'recipients'], 'readwrite', (tx) => {
+  tx.objectStore('notes').delete(id);
+  tx.objectStore('recipients').delete(id);
+});

+# The Daily Grind
+
+A static coffee homepage with a local encrypted delivery-note vault.
+
+## Build and checks
+
+- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
+- `pnpm run build` bundles `src/main.js` into `assets/app.js`.
+- `pnpm run test` runs cryptographic round-trip, tamper, and input validation checks in Node.
+
+Serve the project root over HTTPS (or localhost) with a static host. The committed bundle lets the existing static start command serve the page without a separate development server.
+
+## Encrypted notes
+
+The default hybrid mode uses the Noble X25519 + ML-KEM-768 KEM preset. ML-KEM-768-only and X25519-only modes are also available. Each note gets fresh encapsulation randomness, a 32-byte HKDF salt, and a 12-byte AES-GCM nonce. HKDF-SHA-256 derives a non-extractable AES-256-GCM key, binding a domain-separated transcript hash that includes the recipient public key. Envelope metadata is authenticated as additional data, with a 128-bit tag.
+
+Only encrypted instruction text is written to local storage. The location label, date, and algorithm are public metadata. This is a **local preview**, not an authenticated delivery service: recipient key pairs are generated locally and persisted in IndexedDB. Access to this browser profile allows decryption. Clearing storage can permanently remove keys. Exports contain the encrypted envelope, never recipient private keys. Two clearly labeled example notes are encrypted on first use.
+
+A production integration must provision authenticated delivery-team public keys, keep delivery-team private keys off customer devices, and implement authenticated submission, authorization, key rotation, and retention on the delivery service. The local recipient-key storage is intentionally isolated in `src/main.js`; the envelope encryption functions are in `src/crypto.js`.
+
+Revealed notes are hidden after 30 seconds or when the tab becomes hidden. JavaScript strings and browser storage cannot guarantee secure erasure.
+
+Implementation references: [Noble post-quantum](https://github.com/paulmillr/noble-post-quantum) and [Noble curves](https://github.com/paulmillr/noble-curves).

+import { ml_kem768 } from '@noble/post-quantum/ml-kem.js';
+import { ml_kem768_x25519 } from '@noble/post-quantum/hybrid.js';
+import { x25519 } from '@noble/curves/ed25519.js';
+
+const encoder = new TextEncoder();
+const classical = {
+  keygen: () => x25519.keygen(),
+  encapsulate(publicKey) {
+    const ephemeral = x25519.keygen();
+    try { return { cipherText: ephemeral.publicKey, sharedSecret: x25519.getSharedSecret(ephemeral.secretKey, publicKey) }; }
+    finally { ephemeral.secretKey.fill(0); }
+  },
+  decapsulate: (cipherText, secretKey) => x25519.getSharedSecret(secretKey, cipherText),
+};
+const schemes = { hybrid: ml_kem768_x25519, 'post-quantum': ml_kem768, classical };
+export const modeLabels = { hybrid: 'X25519 + ML-KEM-768', 'post-quantum': 'ML-KEM-768', classical: 'X25519' };
+const b64 = bytes => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes));
+const unb64 = string => Uint8Array.from(atob(string), c => c.charCodeAt(0));
+
+export function generateRecipient(mode) {
+  if (!Object.hasOwn(schemes, mode)) throw new Error('Unknown protection level.');
+  return { id: crypto.randomUUID(), mode, ...schemes[mode].keygen() };
+}
+function authenticatedHeader(note) {
+  return encoder.encode(JSON.stringify({ version: note.version, id: note.id, recipient: note.recipient, mode: note.mode, location: note.location, created: note.created, example: note.example, encapsulation: note.encapsulation, salt: note.salt, iv: note.iv }));
+}
+async function deriveKey(sharedSecret, salt, header, publicKey) {
+  const material = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', sharedSecret, 'HKDF', false, ['deriveKey']);
+  // Bind the complete envelope and the recipient public key into the derivation.
+  const transcriptHash = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new Uint8Array([...header, ...publicKey])));
+  const context = new Uint8Array([...encoder.encode('daily-grind/delivery-notes/v1\0'), ...transcriptHash]);
+  return crypto.subtle.deriveKey({ name: 'HKDF', hash: 'SHA-256', salt, info: context }, material, { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt']);
+}
+export async function encryptNote(text, location, recipient, example = false) {
+  if (!text.trim() || text.length > 500) throw new Error('Please write a note of 1–500 characters.');
+  if (!Object.hasOwn(schemes, recipient.mode)) throw new Error('Unknown protection level.');
+  const { cipherText, sharedSecret } = schemes[recipient.mode].encapsulate(recipient.publicKey);
+  const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12));
+  const salt = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32));
+  const note = { version: 1, id: crypto.randomUUID(), recipient: recipient.id, mode: recipient.mode, location, created: new Date().toISOString(), example, encapsulation: b64(cipherText), salt: b64(salt), iv: b64(iv) };
+  const plaintext = encoder.encode(text);
+  try {
+    const header = authenticatedHeader(note);
+    const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, salt, header, recipient.publicKey);
+    note.ciphertext = b64(new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv, additionalData: header, tagLength: 128 }, key, plaintext)));
+    return note;
+  } finally { sharedSecret.fill(0); plaintext.fill(0); }
+}
+export async function decryptNote(note, recipient) {
+  if (note.version !== 1 || !Object.hasOwn(schemes, note.mode) || note.recipient !== recipient.id || note.mode !== recipient.mode) throw new Error('This note cannot be authenticated.');
+  const sharedSecret = schemes[note.mode].decapsulate(unb64(note.encapsulation), recipient.secretKey);
+  try {
+    const header = authenticatedHeader(note);
+    const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, unb64(note.salt), header, recipient.publicKey);
+    const clear = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv: unb64(note.iv), additionalData: header, tagLength: 128 }, key, unb64(note.ciphertext)));
+    try { return new TextDecoder().decode(clear); } finally { clear.fill(0); }
+  } finally { sharedSecret.fill(0); }
+}

+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { encryptNote, decryptNote, generateRecipient } from './crypto.js';
+
+for (const mode of ['hybrid', 'post-quantum', 'classical']) {
+  test(`${mode}: Unicode round trip, fresh encryption, and tamper rejection`, async () => {
+    const recipient = generateRecipient(mode);
+    const text = 'Side door code: 1234. No doorbell ☕ — merci!';
+    const note = await encryptNote(text, 'Home', recipient);
+    assert.equal(await decryptNote(note, recipient), text);
+    assert.ok(!JSON.stringify(note).includes(text));
+    assert.ok(!Object.hasOwn(note, 'secretKey'));
+    const again = await encryptNote(text, 'Home', recipient);
+    assert.notEqual(note.iv, again.iv);
+    assert.notEqual(note.ciphertext, again.ciphertext);
+    for (const field of ['ciphertext', 'encapsulation', 'salt', 'iv']) {
+      const tampered = { ...note, [field]: (note[field][0] === 'A' ? 'B' : 'A') + note[field].slice(1) };
+      await assert.rejects(decryptNote(tampered, recipient));
+    }
+    for (const [field, value] of [['location', 'Office'], ['id', 'other'], ['created', '2020-01-01'], ['example', true], ['mode', 'unknown'], ['version', 2]]) {
+      await assert.rejects(decryptNote({ ...note, [field]: value }, recipient));
+    }
+    await assert.rejects(decryptNote(note, generateRecipient(mode)));
+  });
+}
+test('invalid notes and unsupported modes are rejected', async () => {
+  const recipient = generateRecipient('hybrid');
+  await assert.rejects(encryptNote('  ', 'Home', recipient));
+  await assert.rejects(encryptNote('x'.repeat(501), 'Home', recipient));
+  assert.throws(() => generateRecipient('other'));
+});

+# Forma landing page
+
+Static HTML and CSS. No build step is required.
+
+The experiment SDK is loaded from the requested URL in the document head with `async` and `blocking="render"`. Supporting browsers delay first paint until script execution finishes. Other browsers use a visibility guard installed before the SDK, with load/error cleanup and a four-second failure timeout. JavaScript-disabled visitors can still view the page.
+
+## Experiment integration contract
+
+The supplied `cdn.example.com` address is a placeholder; no SDK API or implementation was supplied. The integration assumes that the SDK applies DOM changes synchronously during execution. An asynchronous SDK requires its actual completion promise/callback to keep native rendering blocked through variant application and release the fallback at the same point. Script `load` alone cannot guarantee completion of asynchronous initialization. The `experiment:ready` event is provided as a fallback reveal hook, but does not extend native render blocking by itself.
+
+The fallback timeout prioritizes access if the CDN is unavailable. It removes the pending script and reveals the page. Removing an already executing third-party script cannot cancel its queued asynchronous work, so a real asynchronous SDK must also support cancellation to prevent late variant changes after a timeout. For a strict no-flash guarantee under all failure conditions, use a confirmed SDK readiness/cancellation API or server-render the assigned variant.
+
+The signup form validates an email address and reports honestly that registration is not connected; it does not collect or transmit email addresses. Product-preview controls are decorative.
+
+Static checks covered inline JavaScript syntax, unique IDs, anchor targets, and SDK attributes. No browser verification or server startup was performed.

+# Rewards registration integration
+
+This repository serves a static frontend. It does not create accounts or store credentials. The UI only shows success for a JSON `201` response containing `{ "created": true }`. Until the following same-origin service is connected, final submission displays a recoverable service-unavailable message. Personal data stays in the form's DOM until a successful submission or navigation; it is never written to local storage, cookies, analytics, or logs by this frontend.
+
+## Service contract
+
+- `GET /api/rewards/csrf`: respond with JSON `{ "csrfToken": "<cryptographically random session-bound token>" }`. Token length: 32–512 characters. Set a `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` session cookie and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
+- `POST /api/rewards`: accept JSON containing `full_name`, `email`, `password`, `favorite_drink` (`coffee`, `tea`, `both`, or `null`), `marketing` (boolean), `terms` (boolean), and the empty honeypot `website`. Require the token in `X-CSRF-Token`, validate against the issuing session, and check the request origin. Reject invalid/missing tokens; do not enable cross-origin registration.
+- Validate all values on the server: nonblank Unicode name (up to 100 characters), valid email (up to 254), password of 15–128 characters without composition rules, allowed drink enum, and explicit terms agreement. Do not infer marketing consent from membership. Rate-limit attempts, reject nonempty honeypots, and prevent duplicate registrations atomically.
+- Return `201 application/json` with `{ "created": true }` only after the account is saved. Use `403` for invalid/expired CSRF, `429` for rate limits, and a non-201 status for other failures. The frontend does not display untrusted server messages or expose whether an email already exists.
+- Hash passwords using a suitable password hashing function such as Argon2id. Never log request bodies, passwords, CSRF tokens, or complete email addresses. Add email verification and account recovery in the account service.
+- Handle repeated or uncertain requests safely: a timeout can occur after a server commit. Enforce email uniqueness and provide a generic recovery route; never create duplicate accounts.
+
+## Deployment
+
+Serve the page and API over HTTPS and set HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and a response-header CSP including `frame-ancestors 'none'`. The page already provides a restrictive meta CSP with same-origin scripts, styles, connections, and form actions. All UI scripts and CSS are external; user values are rendered with `textContent`.
+
+For a complete no-JavaScript fallback, render a real session-bound token into the hidden `csrf_token` input on the server and accept URL-encoded POST data with the same validation, consent, CSRF checks, and secure response pages. The static page exposes every step when JavaScript is absent; it must never bypass CSRF checks for the fallback.
+
+The Terms, Privacy, and Sign in links use the site's existing route conventions. Publish the actual Rewards Terms at `/rewards-terms` before accepting registrations; these destination pages are outside this static page's scope.

+# The Daily Grind: field INP monitoring
+
+The homepage loads a local, deferred ES module built from `web-vitals/attribution`.
+No third-party CDN or browser profiling session is required.
+
+## Deployment
+
+The repository is a static site and **does not contain an analytics backend**.
+Route `POST /analytics/web-vitals` to your analytics ingestion service, or set
+`meta[name="inp-report-endpoint"]` in `index.html` to its real endpoint before
+deployment. Until a collector is connected, the static host cannot store reports.
+The collector should accept a JSON object and return a successful status (e.g.
+204). Prefer a same-origin route; a cross-origin collector must allow CORS for
+JSON POST requests and be permitted by your `connect-src` CSP.
+An empty endpoint disables monitoring.
+
+Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` after changing
+the source. Commit `assets/inp-monitor.js` and its license file together: the
+checked-in bundle lets the existing static hosting workflow work without a build.
+Serve that asset with revalidation or purge its cache on deployment.
+
+## Reports and analysis
+
+`onINP` is registered once using its normal production reporting behavior. It
+reports the visit's INP when the page becomes hidden, continues tracking on return,
+and creates a new metric ID after a back/forward cache restore. It does not report
+every interaction. Visits without measurable interactions produce no INP report.
+Delivery uses native `fetchLater` with immediate activation when a report is ready;
+the fallback uses keepalive fetch or a beacon. There are no unload handlers,
+polling, synchronous networking, or retries. Network delivery is best effort.
+
+Upsert reports by `id`, retaining the latest `reportedAt` and its **absolute**
+`value`; do not count successive updates as separate visits or add absolute values.
+Compute the 75th percentile over visit values, including good interactions, and
+segment by `navigationType` as appropriate. Ratings follow web-vitals: good at
+200 ms or less, needs improvement up to 500 ms, and poor above 500 ms.
+
+For slow reports, inspect:
+
+- `inputDelay`, `processingDuration`, and `presentationDelay` to locate the delay
+  before event handlers, in handlers, or before the next paint.
+- `interactionTarget` (static `data-inp-target` labels), `interactionType`, and
+  `loadState` to identify the control and loading context.
+- `longestScript` and the top ten overlapping `scripts`: script URL, function,
+  character offset, invoker type, intersecting time, and INP subpart. Script
+  subpart labels use their start relative to the phase boundaries; scripts can
+  span more than one phase. Use source maps for the deployed script version to
+  translate character offsets to source locations.
+- `forcedStyleDuration` and `forcedLayoutDuration` on scripts to distinguish
+  forced style recalculation from synchronous layout. Older implementations expose
+  only the combined `forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration`.
+- `renderStyleDuration` and `renderLayoutDuration` for full rendering-phase totals
+  across relevant long frames. These are full-frame timings, not exact slices of
+  the interaction. `totalStyleAndLayoutDuration` provides the library's combined
+  fallback, including forced work; avoid adding it to the separate totals.
+- `totalScriptDuration`, `totalPaintDuration`, and `totalUnattributedDuration` for
+  the library's remaining attribution breakdown. Paint is a timing estimate,
+  not a GPU profiler; small discrepancies from Event Timing rounding can occur.
+
+Unsupported or unavailable timing fields are `null`, not zero. `loafSupported`
+and `loafCount` distinguish absent API support from no matching long frames.
+Browsers without Long Animation Frames still report INP and its three phases;
+browsers without Event Timing cannot report INP. LoAF exposes only long frames
+and scripts above its reporting threshold, so attribution indicates likely
+contributors rather than proving causation or capturing every script.
+
+Payloads omit raw performance entries, DOM selectors, text, input values, page
+queries, and script URL queries/fragments/credentials. Script details are bounded
+and truncated to the ten largest overlaps (`scriptsTruncated` flags omissions).
+The page identifier is the fixed homepage route `/`.
+
+Tests run entirely in Node, covering serialization, phase attribution, unsupported
+timings, payload bounds, and transport fallback behavior. They do not start a
+server or perform browser verification.

+# The Daily Grind: field INP monitoring
+
+The homepage loads `assets/inp.js`, a local bundle of Google's
+[`web-vitals` attribution build](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals#attribution).
+No external analytics script is fetched at runtime. The page design is unchanged.
+
+## Connect a collector
+
+This repository serves static files and has no ingestion backend. Set the
+`inp-report-endpoint` meta tag in `index.html` to your deployed same-origin
+collector, for example:
+
+```html
+<meta name="inp-report-endpoint" content="/analytics/vitals">
+```
+
+The collector must accept JSON POSTs. This example route is **not** provided by
+the static site. With an empty endpoint, monitoring still produces a local
+snapshot and event, but no data is sent remotely. Configure the endpoint when
+deploying to aggregate real-user results.
+
+Reports use `sendBeacon`, with `fetch({ keepalive: true })` when beacon queuing
+fails. Delivery is best effort; a queued beacon does not acknowledge ingestion.
+There are no automatic retries. Ensure the site's `connect-src` policy permits
+the collector. Responses do not affect navigation.
+
+## Report contract and analysis
+
+- `id` identifies the page-lifetime INP metric; `sequence` orders updates. Upsert
+  by `id` and keep the greatest sequence, rather than counting each update as a
+  new visit. Back/forward cache restoration is handled by `web-vitals` with a new
+  metric ID. Compute p75 over each visit's latest `value`, in milliseconds.
+- `value`, `delta`, `rating`, and `navigationType` preserve the library's metric.
+  All changed INP candidates are reported, including good values. `slow` means
+  INP exceeds 200 ms. This measures page-level INP, not a log of every interaction.
+- `interaction` identifies the control through static `data-inp-target` labels,
+  the input type, timestamps, and load state. It does not include typed values,
+  DOM nodes, link text, or dynamic selector IDs.
+- `phases` separates input delay, event processing, and presentation delay.
+  `longestScript` records its matching phase (`subpart`), intersecting duration,
+  source URL, function, character position, invocation type, and forced layout.
+- `rendering` preserves the library's estimates for script, style/layout, paint,
+  and unattributed time. These overlap the phase breakdown; do not add them to
+  the phases. They are not exact profiler measurements.
+- `frames` contains up to five overlapping Long Animation Frames, ordered by
+  duration, each with its five longest scripts. Frame timing includes blocking,
+  rendering start, and style/layout start. Counts indicate truncation. The
+  library's longest script is retained independently of these limits.
+
+Group slow reports by control, phase, script URL/function, and forced layout
+duration to identify recurring contributors. Overlapping scripts are attribution
+evidence, not proof that each script caused the whole interaction delay.
+Script URLs omit query strings, fragments, and credentials. The page is recorded
+as `/`, without a visitor identifier or the page URL's query parameters.
+
+INP requires Event Timing support and user interaction; visits without a
+measurable interaction do not produce an INP value. `web-vitals` handles page
+visibility changes and back/forward cache lifecycle reporting. LoAF attribution

+reporting threshold, cross-origin scripts, and other unavailable work may be
+missing. `attributionStatus` distinguishes `unsupported`, `no-long-frame`, and
+`available`. Missing rendering estimates are `null`, not zero.

+`event.detail`. The most recent serialized report is also stored at
+`sessionStorage.getItem('daily-grind:inp')`; storage failure is ignored.
+

+
+```sh
+pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+pnpm build
+pnpm test
+```
+
+Commit the generated `assets/inp.js` with source changes so the existing static
+hosting command can serve the instrumentation without a runtime build step.
+Tests cover report attribution, unavailable APIs, payload limits, URL sanitation,
+endpoint validation, and beacon/fetch transport. No browser or server is needed.

@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+## Scope and evidence
+
+Audited the complete supplied site: one static HTML document, inline CSS, system fonts,
+13 native navigation links, and one external CSS background image. There are no runtime
+scripts, frameworks, hydration, analytics, interaction handlers, build pipeline, or backend
+in this repository. No browser, development/preview server, or server entrypoint was used.
+
+This is a source and asset audit, not a Lighthouse run or a field measurement. LCP, INP,
+CLS, TTFB, and performance scores cannot be reported from these checks. The hero is a
+likely LCP candidate; the actual LCP element depends on viewport and rendering.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Area | Finding | Implemented change |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LCP discovery | The hero was a CSS background with no priority hint. | A parser-discoverable `picture` / `img` uses `fetchpriority="high"` and eager loading. No redundant preload is needed for an image present in the initial HTML. |
+| Image transfer | Every device requested the same remote 1350px image. | Five local WebP variants, mobile art direction, width descriptors, and `sizes="100vw"` let the browser select one candidate. |
+| Network dependency | The hero required a connection to Unsplash at runtime. | Images are served from the site's origin. No third-party page requests remain. |
+| Layout stability | The hero already had a reserved height; mobile browser chrome could change viewport geometry. | Keep reserved hero space, add image/source dimensions, and use `60svh` with a `60vh` fallback and a 320px minimum. |
+| Mobile interaction | A single-row navigation could overflow, making links difficult to reach. | Wrap navigation, stack it on narrow screens, and give navigation/footer links a minimum 44px height. Let the card grid shrink below 250px when necessary. |
+| Keyboard and motion | No explicit keyboard focus treatment or reduced-motion support. | Visible focus rings and reduced-motion rules for the existing color transitions. |
+| INP / main thread | No JavaScript or expensive interaction handlers exist in the supplied page. | Keep native links and zero runtime JavaScript. No speculative workers, routing, or monitoring libraries added. |
+| FCP / fonts / CSS | Critical CSS is small and inline; fonts are local system fonts. | Retain this architecture and avoid additional blocking requests or font swaps. |
+
+The original image remains the stock photo used by the site. Its URL and the exact
+download URLs, dimensions, and byte sizes of the optimized assets are recorded in
+`assets/image-manifest.json`. No generated imagery was used.
+
+## Asset measurements
+
+The original image URL returned **157,968 bytes** when fetched for this audit. Its
+`auto=format` response may vary with client format negotiation; this is a downloaded
+asset comparison, not a capture of a browser's original network request.
+
+| Candidate | Dimensions | Bytes | Difference from downloaded original |
+| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
+| Mobile, small | 480 × 600 | 44,754 | 71.7% smaller |
+| Mobile, large | 800 × 1000 | 100,570 | 36.3% smaller |
+| Desktop, small | 960 × 480 | 58,054 | 63.3% smaller |
+| Desktop, medium | 1440 × 720 | 114,552 | 27.5% smaller |
+| Desktop, large | 1920 × 960 | 203,850 | 29.0% larger |
+
+The largest candidate offers additional resolution for wide/high-density displays; it
+is intentionally larger than the original. Browser choice depends on viewport width,
+device pixel ratio, and browser heuristics. The variants are alternatives, not five
+images downloaded per initial visit. Mobile crops avoid downloading pixels far outside
+the portrait hero. Image positioning and the dark overlay preserve the existing design.
+
+## Automated verification
+
+Run `npm test` (Node.js built-ins only; no installation or server required).
+The five checks enforce:
+
+- HTML budgets of 10 KiB raw and 3 KiB gzip.
+- No scripts, external stylesheets, remote image URLs, or web-font declarations.
+- High-priority eager hero loading, reserved space, responsive candidates, and valid descriptors.
+- Local WebP container integrity, actual pixel dimensions, manifest accuracy, and size budgets:
+  50 KiB for the smallest mobile asset, 120 KiB through 1440px, 205 KiB maximum.
+- All 13 native navigation links and the responsive wrapping/grid rules.
+
+All five checks pass. These checks protect the source-level performance improvements;
+they do not emulate browser layout or measure user interaction latency. The static
+site has no build script, so no build was required.
+
+## Hosting and remaining validation
+
+The repository does not contain production hosting configuration. Configure HTML
+compression (Brotli or gzip) and revalidation at the actual host. WebP is already
+compressed and does not need additional gzip. Cache these unversioned image URLs with
+revalidation or a moderate TTL; use content-hashed filenames before adopting year-long
+`immutable` caching. Confirm correct `image/webp` MIME types, HTTPS, CDN behavior,
+and document response time in the deployed environment.
+
+The linked menu, account, checkout, and other destination routes have no implementation
+in this repository. Their server latency, scripts, and interaction behavior cannot be
+audited here; all existing destinations are preserved.
+
+When deployed performance data is available, assess the 75th percentile separately for
+mobile and desktop against LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, and CLS ≤ 0.1. Use existing field
+analytics or CrUX/PageSpeed Insights for the deployed origin. No passing Core Web Vitals
+claim is made without that data.
+
+References: [Optimize LCP](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-lcp/),
+[Image performance](https://web.dev/learn/images/performance-issues/),
+[Web Vitals](https://web.dev/articles/vitals).
